title: Keep the sandbox seam; one policy for every enforcing capability
Sandbox backends per operating system: bubblewrap then Landlock, Seatbelt, Windows restricted token
The launcher is the harness binary; launcher status travels out of band
A plugin process is untrusted and holds only granted capabilities
Approval flow: closed outcomes, fail closed, attributed audit

Browser authentication for the HTML UI
Remote clients: Peers, principals and mandatory access declarations

Security controls are proven on the real entry path, and configuration is strict
The harness is stated as unaudited until an independent security review is done (answers UP-DEBT-found.Q3.1)
The unaudited statement appears on the safety page, in the operator guide and in dsh sandbox status, and no text calls the harness secure, safe or isolated without it

reason: Both causes are JavaScript mechanisms that the Go design does not have: the Loader unwrapping a module to its default export and losing the dependency list, and a property proxy whose service lookup walks ancestors only. Go components are compiled in and declare dependencies by type (DH-ADR-4), and the process gap that let 178 tests miss it is closed by requiring tests through the real loader path (DH-ADR-SECURITY-11 b).

The cause was a YAML expression object accepted where a boolean was expected and read as truthy, plus a snapshot check that accepted an unknown-tool result. Strict configuration decoding makes a non-boolean disabled value a load error and an independent check rejects calls to unregistered tools (DH-ADR-SECURITY-11 c, d); file and shell tools share one sandbox policy, so no permission preset governs only half of them (DH-ADR-SECURITY-1).

The agent did not know which URL and process served its session and mistook a bare Vite development server returning HTTP 200 for the application. The Go host renders and serves the UI from one binary with no separate client development server (DH-ADR-3), and it publishes its single canonical origin to the model context and tool environment (DH-ADR-SECURITY-7 d).

The cause was attributing launcher failure from the confined command's stderr text and exit code, an in-band channel shared with the child. The Go launcher reports its status on a separate inherited pipe that closes at exec, so a child's exit code or output can never be read as launcher failure (DH-ADR-SECURITY-3), and each backend needs a deterministic fake at the OS boundary plus a real-kernel scenario that is not allowed to count as passed when skipped (DH-ADR-SECURITY-11 a).
